title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
statement: Return the length of the longest palindromic subsequence of `s`.
hints: A subsequence does not have to be contiguous. This is not the longest palindromic substring.
If the ends match, add 2 to the answer for the inside.
If they differ, drop one end. The answer is the LCS of s and its reverse.

approaches.name: Interval DP
approaches.explanation: dp[i][j] is the answer on s[i:j+1].

approaches.name: LCS with the reverse
approaches.explanation: A palindromic subsequence is a common subsequence of s and reverse(s).

editorial: The LCS formulation is the shortest proof. Any palindromic subsequence reads the same forward and backward, so it is common to s and reverse(s), and the longest such common subsequence can be realized as a palindrome. The interval DP writes the same recurrence without building the reverse explicitly.
